novels.title: The Moonlit Teahouse
novels.desc: A quiet teahouse, a mysterious customer, and a story that keeps unfolding after sunset.

chapters.title: The Guest After Midnight
text: Rain had been falling since dusk, turning the stone road outside the teahouse into a ribbon of silver.
By the time the last lantern was lit, everyone had gone home—everyone except the stranger sitting in the corner.
She had ordered only tea. Yet somehow, she had been waiting for him.
He looked up when the bell above the door rang. For a moment, neither of them spoke.
Then he smiled, as though they had met a very long time ago.

chapters.title: A Name Written in Tea
text: The next morning, she found a folded piece of paper beneath the teapot.
There was only a name written on it.
She read it twice before realizing that she already knew whom it belonged to.

novels.title: Spring in September
novels.desc: An original story about two strangers, a second-hand bookstore, and the strange comfort of meeting someone at the right time.

chapters.title: The Bookstore on Willow Street
text: The bookstore was smaller than Mina expected.
It had no sign, no website, and no particular reason to be open on a rainy Tuesday afternoon.
A little bell chimed overhead. Somewhere between the shelves, someone laughed.

chapters.title: The Umbrella
text: He held the umbrella over both of them without asking.
It was an ordinary kindness, but Mina remembered it all the way home.

novels.title: Jade After Snow
novels.desc: A cultivator returns to a mountain that should have forgotten her—and discovers it remembers everything.

chapters.title: The Mountain Gate
text: Snow covered the mountain gate, but the old inscription was still visible.
She placed one hand against the stone and whispered the name she had sworn never to speak again.

chapters.title: The Empty Pavilion
text: There was no one in the pavilion.
There were, however, fresh footprints in the snow.
